questions.q: The set of values of $a$~for which $\lim_{x \to a} \left(  \left[$x - 5\right] - \left[$2x + 2\right]\right) = 0$, where,~\left[$ζ\right]$~denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to~$ζ& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$\lim_{x \to a}\left(\left[x - 5\right] - \left[2x + 2\right]\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to a}\left(\left[x\right] - 5 - \left[2x\right] - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to a}\left(\left[x\right] - \left[2x\right] - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to a}\left(\left[x\right] - \left[2x\right]\right) = 7$

Now when~$a \in I$~(integer) then~$a - 2a = 7 ⇒ a = - 7$

Now when~$a \in I + f$~where~$f$~is fraction,

So,~\left[I + f\right] - \left[2I + 2f\right] = 7$

$⇒ I + \left[f\right] - 2I - \left[2f\right] = 7$

$⇒ I + 0 - 2I - \left[2f\right] = 7$

$⇒ - I - \left[2f\right] = 7$

Now taking case~\left(1\right)$~when~$f \in \left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Then~$⇒ - I - 0 = 7 ⇒ I = - 7 ⇒ a \in \left(-7, - 6 . 5\right)$

Now taking case~ \left($2\right)$~when~$f \in \left(\dfrac{1}{2},$1\right)$

So,~$- I - 1 = 7 ⇒ I = - 8 ⇒ a \in \left(-$7 . 5, 7\right)$

Hence, from both the cases we can say that~$a \in \left(- 7 . 5, - 6 . 5\right).

$

Apply $L$'Hospital Rule

$\lim_{x \to 2} \left(\dfrac{2xf \left($2\right) - 4f^{'}\left($x\right)}{1}\right)

$= \dfrac{4\left(4\right) - 4}{1} =12

questions.solution:
This limit is ${1}^{\infty}$ form

$∴ \lim_{x \to 0}{\left(\dfrac{1 + f\left(3 + x\right) - f\left(3\right)}{1 + f\left(2 - x\right) - f\left(2\right)}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{x}} = e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{x}\left(\dfrac{1 + f\left(3 + x\right) - f\left(3\right)}{1 + f\left(2 - x\right) - f\left(2\right)} - 1\right)}$

$= e^{0} = 1.

$

$\begin{aligned} & L=\frac{\left\{1-\frac{(2 x)^2}{\underline{2}}+\frac{(2 x)^4}{\underline{4} \cdots\}\}+a\left\{1-\frac{(4 x)^2}{\underline{2}}+\frac{(4 x)^4}{\lfloor 4} \ldots \cdot\right\}-b}\right.}{x^4} \\ & L=\frac{(1+a-b)-x^2(2+8 a)+x^4\left(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{32}{3} a\right)+x^6() \ldots}{x^4}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 1+\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}=0 \text { and } 2+8 \mathrm{a}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=-\frac{1}{4} \\ & \mathrm{~b}=\mathrm{a}+1 \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}+1=\frac{3}{4} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{3}{4}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4}$ and $b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{1 + \cos x}}$, then the value of $ab^{3}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}} - 2}{x^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + x^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} - 1}{x^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + 0}} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} - 1}{x^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + 1} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} - 1}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} - 1}{x4} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} + 1}{\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} + 1}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 + x^{4} - 1}{x^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + x^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{x^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + 0} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{x^{4}\left(2\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$

Also, $b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{1 + \cos x}}$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - \cos^{2}x\right) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + \cos x} )}{2 - ( 1 + \cos x )}$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(1 - \cos x\right)\left(1 + \cos x\right) ( $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + \cos x} )\left($1 - \cos x\right)$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0} ( 1 + \cos x ) ( $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + \cos x} )

$⇒ b = ( 1 + \cos 0 ) ( $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + \cos 0} )

$⇒ b = ( 1 + 1 ) ( $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + 1} )

$⇒ b = ( 2 ) ( $2\sqrt{2} )

$⇒ b = $4\sqrt{2}

$⇒ ab^{3} = $\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \times (((4\sqrt{2}{)}^{3}

$⇒ ab^{3} = 32

$

questions.q: Let& $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax - \left(e^{3x} - 1\right)}{\alphax\left(e^{3x} - 1\right)}$~for some~$\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the value of~$\alpha + \beta$& is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax - \left(e^{3x} - 1\right)}{\alphax\left(e^{3x} - 1\right)} = \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax + 1 - e^{3x}}{\dfrac{\alphax\left(e^{3x} - 1\right)}{3x} \cdot 3x} = \beta$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alphax + 1 - e^{3x}}{3\alphax^{2}} = \beta$~as~ \left(\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{x} - 1}{x} = 1\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha - 3e^{3x}}{6\alphax} = \beta$ [Using L' Hospital rule~as~ \left(\dfrac{0}{0}\text{form}\right)$]

Now for limit to exist, $\alpha = 3$

So,~$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{3 - 3e^{3x}}{6 \times 3 \times x} = \beta$

So,~$\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- \left(e^{3x} - 1\right)}{6x} = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- 3e^{3x}}{6} = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \alpha + \beta = \dfrac{5}{2}$

questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(2 x^2-3 x+5\right)(3 x-1)^{\frac{x}{2}}}{\left(3 x^2+5 x+4\right) \sqrt{(3 x+2)^x}}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(2 x^2-3 x+5\right)(3 x-1)^{x / 2}}{\left(3 x^2+5 x+4\right) \sqrt{(3 x+2)^x}} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{x^2\left(2-\frac{3}{x}+\frac{5}{x^2}\right)(3 x)^{\frac{x}{2}}}{x^2\left(3+\frac{5}{x}+\frac{4}{x^2}\right)(3 x)^{\frac{x}{2}}} \cdot \frac{\left(1-\frac{1}{3 x}\right)^{\frac{x}{2}}}{\left(1+\frac{2}{3 x}\right)^{\frac{x}{2}}} \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(1-\frac{1}{3 x}\right)^{\frac{x}{2}}=e^{\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(1-\frac{1}{3 x}-1\right) \times \frac{x}{2}}=e^{\frac{-1}{6}} \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(1+\frac{2}{3 x}\right)=e^{\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(1+\frac{2}{3 x}-1\right) \times \frac{x}{2}} \\
& =e^{\frac{1}{3}}
\end{aligned}$
So, $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{e^{\frac{-1}{6}}}{e^{\frac{1}{3}}}=\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{e^{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}}}=\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{e}}$

questions.q: Let  \left[t\right]$ denote the greatest integer $\le t$. If $\lambdaεR - \left\{0, 1\right\}, \lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$, then $L$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - x + \left|x\right|}{\lambda - x + \left[x\right]}\right| = L$

Let's find left-hand and right-hand limit.

For left-hand limit

$x = 0 - h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - \left(- h\right) + \left|- h\right|}{\lambda - \left(- h\right) + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h - \left(- h\right)}{\lambda + h + \left[- h\right]}\right|$

Since~$h > 0 ⇒ \left[- h\right] = - 1$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h - 1}\right| = 1\left|\lambda - 1\right|$

For right-hand limit

$x = 0 + h, x \to 0, h \to 0, h > 0$

$RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 - h + \left|h\right|}{\lambda - h + \left[h\right]}\right|$

Since~$h > 0 ⇒ \left[h\right] = 0$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\left|\dfrac{1 + h + h}{\lambda + h + 0}\right| = 1\left|\lambda\right|$

For existence of limit~$LHL = RHL$

$⇒ 1\left|\lambda - 1\right| = 1\left|\lambda\right|$

Cross multiply and square both side.

$⇒ {λ}^{2} = \left(\lambda - 1\right)2 ⇒ {λ}^{2} = {λ}^{2} + 1 - 2\lambda$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Limit~$L = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2$

questions.q: If $\lim_{x \to \infty}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} - ax\right) = b$, then the ordered pair $( a, b )$ is:

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} - ax\right) \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} + ax}{\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} + ax} = b$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{\left(x^{2} - x + 1\right) - ( ax{)}^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} + ax} = b$

$⇒ \text{Limit exist only If}a^{2} = 1$,~because~$x^{2}$~must not be there in the numerator~

$∴ a = 1, - 1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{- x + 1}{\sqrt{x^{2} - x + 1} + ax} = b$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{- 1 + \dfrac{1}{x}}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}} + a} = b$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{1 + a} = b$

Here,~$a \ne - 1$

So$a = 1$

$b = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

$( a, b ) ≡ \left($1, \dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

!$

questions.solution: RHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(x-0)^{2}}{x^{2}}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right.}{x^{2}}+1\right)=1+\pi$ And LHL is, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+(-x+\sin x)^{2}}{x^{2}}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{\tan \left(\pi \sin ^{2} x\right)+x^{2}+\sin ^{2} x-2 x \sin x}{x^{2}}=\pi+1+1-2=\pi$ Since, LHL ≠ RHL Hence, limit does not exist.

questions.q: $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,

$L = \lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\}$

Now,

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3} < 1$

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5} < 1$

--------------------

$2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1} < 1 \forall n \in N$

And ${\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right) < {\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < \lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\} < \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

$⇒ \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} < L < \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n}$

And $\lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{n} = 0 \text{ and } \lim_{n \to \infty}{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)}^{n} = 0$

$\left\{\text{as}2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3} < 1 \text{ and } 2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1} < 1\right\}$

Hence, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\left\{\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{5}\right) . . . . \left(2\dfrac{1}{2} - 2\dfrac{1}{2n + 1}\right)\right\} = 0$

questions.q: If $\alpha = \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\tan^{3}x - \tan x}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$ and $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\cos x\right)\cot x$ are the roots of the equation, $ax^{2} + bx - 4 = 0,$~then the ordered pair  \left(a, b\right)$ is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
If,& $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\cos x\right)\cot x$~ ~ (${1}^{\infty}$form)

$\beta = e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\cot x\left[\cos x - 1\right]}$

$\beta = e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- \cos x}{\sin x}\left[1 - 1 + 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}$

$\beta = e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- \cos x}{2sin\dfrac{x}{2} . cos\dfrac{x}{2}}\left[1 - 1 + 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}$

$\beta = e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- \cos x . sin\dfrac{x}{2}}{cos\dfrac{x}{2}}}$

$\beta = e^{0}$

$\beta = 1$
$\alpha = \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\tan^{3}x - \tan x}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\tan x ( \tan x + 1 ) ( \tan x - 1 )}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$\alpha = \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\tan x \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\left(\tan x + 1\right) \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{( \tan x - 1 )}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$\alpha = 1 \times \left(1 + 1\right) \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{( \tan x - 1 )}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= 2\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\tan x - 1}{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= 2\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\sin x - \cos x}{\cos x . \cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= - 2\sqrt{2}\lim_{x \to \pi / 4} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}$\cos x - $\dfrac{1}{2}$\sin x\right)\cos x . \cos \left($x + $\dfrac{π}{4}\right)

\alpha = -$2$\sqrt{2}\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{\cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}{\cos x . \cos \left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}

\alpha = -$4$

So, the equation whose roots are \alpha and \beta is

$x^{2} + 3x - 4 = 0$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right)$~be a polynomial function such that $f\left(x\right) + f^{'}\left(x\right) + f^{' '}\left(x\right) = x^{5} + 64$. Then, the value of $\lim_{x \to 1}\d$dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x - 1}$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $f \left(x\right) = \left($x - 1\right)\left($x^{4} + ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + d\right)$

f\left($x\right) + f^{'}\left($x\right) + f^{''}\left($x\right) = x^{5} + \left($a + 4\right)x^{4} + \left($b + 3a + 16\right)x^{3} +$

\left(9a + 2b + c - 12\right)x^{2} + \left($d + c + 4b - 6a\right)x + \left($c - 2b\right)$

$∵ $f\left($x\right) + f^{'}\left($x\right) + f^{''}\left($x\right) = x^{5} + 64$

$⇒ a + 4 = 0, b + 3a + 16 = 0, 9a + 2b + c - 12 = 0, d + c + 4b - 6a = 0$

$⇒ a = - 4, b = - 4, c = 56, d = - 64$

So~$\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{f \left($x\right)}{x - 1} = \lim_{x \to 1} \left(x^{4} - 4x^{3} - 4x^{2} + 56x - 64\right)$

$= 1 - 4 - 4 + 56 - 64 = - 15

$

$= \lim_{x \to {2}^{+}}\sqrt{2} \cdot \left|\sin\left(\dfrac{x^{2} - x - 2}{2}\right)\right|x - 2$

$= \lim_{x \to {2}^{+}}\sqrt{2} \cdot \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{x^{2} - x - 2}{2}\right)}{x - 2}$~(because~$x > 2$)

$= \lim_{x \to {2}^{+}}\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \left($x - 2\right)\left(x + 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}.$

questions.q: If the value of $\lim_{x \to 0} \left(2 - \cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}\right)\left(\dfrac{x + 2}{x2}\right) is equal to $e^{a}$, then $a$ \text{ and } is equal to_____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(2 - \cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}\right)\left(\dfrac{x + 2}{x2}\right) \to {1}^{∞}$

Hence,
$= e^{\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x2}\right) \times \left(x + 2\right)}$
Now,

$\lim_{x \to 0} \left(\dfrac{1 - \cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x2}\right) \to \left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)

Using L'Hospital Rule

$\lim_{x \to 0} \left\{\dfrac{\sin x\sqrt{\cos 2x} - \cos x \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\cos 2x}} \times \left(- 2\sin 2x\right)}{2x}\right
~

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \left\{\dfrac{\sin x \cos 2x + \sin 2x \cdot \cos x}{2x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}\right

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \left\{\dfrac{\sin 3x}{2x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}\right

=\dfrac{3}{2}\lim_{x \to 0} \left\${\dfrac{\sin 3x}{3x}\right\times \lim_{x \to 0} \left\{\dfrac{1}{\cos 2x}\right\}$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}\lim_{x \to 0} \left\{\dfrac{\sin 3x}{3x}\right \times1$

=\dfrac{3}{2}

So,

$e^{\lim_{x \to $0}\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos x\sqrt{\cos 2x}}{x2}\right)\left($x + 2\right)}$

=e^{\dfrac{3}{2} \times2}$ = e^{3}$

$⇒ a = 3$

questions.q: Let&  \left[t\right]$ denote the greatest integer $\le t$~and~\left\{t\right\}$~denote the fractional part of $t$. Then integral value of $\alpha$~for which the left hand limit of the function $f\left(x\right) = \left[1 + x\right] + \dfrac{{α}^{2\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}} + \left[x\right] - 1}{2\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}}$~at $x = 0$~is equal to $\alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}& is _____$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left[1 + x\right] + \dfrac{{α}^{2\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}} + \left[x\right] - 1}{2\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}}$

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}f\left(x\right) = \alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\left[1 + x\right] + \dfrac{{α}^{\left[x\right] + \left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}} + \left[x\right] - 1}{2\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\}} = \alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ 0 + \dfrac{{α}^{- 1} - 2}{- 1} = \alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ 2 - \dfrac{1}{α} = \alpha - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \dfrac{1}{α} = \dfrac{10}{3}$

On solving above equation we get,

$⇒ \alpha = 3; \alpha \in I$
